items.raw_excerpt: Norway has released its first national guidelines on screen use for children and young people from birth to 18 years old. Here’s what parents should keep in mind to protect your kids, from tiny toddlers to teens.

items.raw_excerpt: We don't want to be a Cassandra, but you really should believe us about this phrase.
items.summary_en: Fare la Cassandra means to warn people about a coming problem or disaster. It comes from Cassandra of Greek mythology, who made true bad predictions that nobody believed. Italians use it when someone keeps warning about bad things to come.

During this last class of Both’s current one-week intensive Dutch language course, eight students – Both’s maximum per course – sit around a huge white table that takes...
items.summary_en: A small language school in Amsterdam offers intensive one-week Dutch courses. Students learn through conversation and games in a cozy classroom on the Keizersgracht canal. The school keeps classes to just eight students to make learning personal and fun.

items.raw_excerpt: Researchers in Nijmegen have set up a laboratory to try to answer one of the oldest questions known to science: why are people ticklish? Aristotle, Erasmus, Galileo and Darwin all tried to put their finger on the purpose of tickling, or gargalesis to use its scientific name, without finding a definitive reason. Now two researchers at Radboud University in Nijmegen are using robots and sensors to try to shed more light on the phenomenon. Tickling exists across cultures and throughout...
items.summary_en: Researchers at Radboud University in Nijmegen, Netherlands, have built a robot to study why people are ticklish. Aristotle, Galileo, and Darwin all tried to answer this question, but no one found a definitive reason yet. The team uses sensors and a robot arm to explore this age-old mystery in a new way.

items.raw_excerpt: The Sock It To MND campaign supports the ex-rugby league star's final epic fundraising challenge.
items.summary_en: Former rugby league player Kevin Sinfield is selling 7,777 limited-edition pairs of socks to raise money for motor neurone disease charities. The campaign supports his final fundraising challenge, running an ultra marathon every day for seven days across England. All profits from sock sales go directly to MND causes.
